title: Alberta Hunter engagement and the Remember My Name film
summary: Hall worked with Alberta Hunter until it ended unfairly, then recorded and served as music coordinator on Robert Altman's film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So then, when you came back from that tour, what did you start doing, just things here --

Just things here and there, until I -- that was in May. And then I was working in New Jersey and places like that. O'Connors in New Jersey, that's a jazz spot, a New Jersey jazz club. Just stayed here until I went with Alberta.
Now, when was that? When did you go with Alberta?
In October.
Yeah, year before last -- year before this. I'm getting my years mixed up. And you were with Alberta until the Fiasco.
Yeah, up until the Fiasco.
Uh-huh. Well, would you like to talk about that?
Not right now. I'd like to pick it up
a little later.
All right.
I'd like to --
In context, you mean?
Yeah. Well, maybe not.
Well, whatever, you know, whatever sequence you want to talk about it in. But it certainly has bearing on the way you are right now.
Right. It has bearing on the people that I'm working with. Well, just say that my engagement was unfairly closed at an unexpected time. That's the end of the Alberta Hunter era.
You did do a record date with her, though?
Yes, just released -- haven't heard it yet -- and a picture.
Picture for Robert Altman.
Right, Robert Allman, called "Remember My Name" with Geraldine Chaplin and Robert . We did all the music for the sound track, and I was the musical coordinator of that project.
